name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.185.0 — Merging a spec worktree now commits the run-log rows and retained evidence it copies onto main (chore(ledger): record <spec> build and review rows), limited to those two paths and skipped when they are git-ignored or unchanged. Before this, those copied files stayed uncommitted and the next spec's merge refused with "root working tree is dirty" (hit twice on 2026-09-14). 7.184.0 — A note is a conversation: turnOf(n) in lib/mocks-notes.js is the one derivation of whose turn it is (session/you/done/dropped) off status/resolution/addressed/reply, replacing four separate per-surface colour rules; the owner may reply on the page as often as they like (POST /__notes/reopen now refuses only a resolved note), the CLI's now-redundant reply subcommand and its writer are deleted in favor of one session verb (notes address), and POST /__notes/resolve requires an explicit verdict so Approve and Reject write different records — Reject is final and hidden from every page. notes open now lists only what waits on the session. ADR-0026 narrows specs/20260912/12 D17, specs/20260902/10 D4 and specs/20260912/06's row controls. 7.183.0 — The review driver no longer parks a CLEAN close at REPLAY: DONE follows MERGE directly every time, the replay-recorded mark and its REPLAY state are deleted (spec-review-driver.js, spec/scripts/lib/parse-selection.js and its test removed), and replay dueness moves into the shared ledger library (lib/observation.js's replayDueness, shared by replay.js --due and the dashboard) alongside a new specs-done-since-last-release derivation (sinceLastRelease). /spec:status's footer now shows a `· N done since last release` or `· N done, never released` clause plus a `· replay due (r/5) — /spec:replay` clause, both ignorable and neither ever blocking anything — /spec:replay is the sole executor. docs/adr/0025 records the reversal: a block on an already-finished review is bypassed anyway, and the earlier printed-reminder measurement (12+ skipped reviews) is now why dueness lives on the dashboard instead of in a report.
